about: Test vectors for the strength function f (Blueprint §6, issue #15).
These are the executable half of the specification. They are data rather than
Go so that a second implementation — a verifier written by someone else, in
another language — can be held to the same answers. If f and these disagree,
one of them is a bug and the disagreement is the finding.
Unless a case says otherwise, the definition is the bednet definition from
tests/fixtures/world.yaml: ceiling 3, three rules descending to a floor.

cases.name: national system of record, anchored worker, all fields — the strongest thing this definition awards
same evidence, contact-verified worker — identity assurance alone drops it a tier
cases.why: Tier 1's stated primary risk is identity mapping error (§4.1). The evidence did not get weaker; the claim that this worker is the one it describes did.

cases.name: programme system, digital capture, one field, contact-verified
the floor: self-reported, unsupervised, no optional fields, no identity binding
cases.why: §8 says a record providing only the mandatory core is valid Tier-1-capable evidence. This is that sentence as a test.

cases.name: a missing required field drops the rule, it does not fail the record
a compromised source is downgraded on assessment alone, with no reissuance
cases.why: The credential is unchanged and still says exactly what it said. What changed is how the deployment regards the source today (§6).

assessment.reason: under investigation after a bulk edit

cases.name: an assessment can take a source below what the definition recognises at all
cases.why: Not tier 0. Calling it tier 0 invites someone to store it as a number, and a stored zero is a stored judgement.

cases.name: the definition's ceiling caps evidence that would otherwise earn more
a definition with no floor can reject a record outright
cases.why: Definitions are allowed to be strict. What they are not allowed to do is be strict by accident, which is why the fixture definition's floor is asserted separately.

cases.name: an external institution's own system record is capped at tier 2 — and it is still the letterhead that earns less (G1 #8, §16)
cases.why: Tier 3 says the record came from a system whose capture this deployment can account for, and an external institution's account of its own capture is one nobody here can check — there is no source-class accreditation to check it against. This narrows G1 #8 rather than reversing it: the distinction that case existed to make, between a system record and a letter on letterhead, survives at 2 against 1 instead of 3 against 1. Revisit when accreditation exists.

cases.name: the same institution, hand-keyed — who the source is does not make a typed row a system record
the cap is on the source class, not on everybody — a programme system still reaches what its rule awards
cases.why: The external-institution ceiling narrows one class. A change that quietly lowered every tier would pass a test that only checked the capped case, and the symptom would be every worker's record reading weaker than it is.

about: The four transports never influence strength (§8). Run one set of facts
through all four and the answer must not move. This is separate from the
cases above because it is a property, not an example: if it ever fails, the
fix is in f, not in a vector.
